definition: A name for the land used in Haudenosaunee tradition, taken from the creation story in which earth grows on the turtle's back. Many other nations use the name too, each in their own way.

The confederacy of the Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga, Seneca and Tuscarora nations, whose homeland lies in what is now New York State, Ontario and Quebec. The name means People of the Longhouse; Iroquois is a name given by others.

The name the Navajo people use for themselves, often translated as the People. Their homeland, Diné Bikéyah, lies in the Four Corners region of the southwestern United States and is governed by the Navajo Nation.

One of the peoples of the Oceti Sakowin, or Great Sioux Nation, whose homeland is the northern Great Plains. Lakota is often translated as allies or friends, and the people are also called Teton Sioux.

A nation of southeast Alaska and the Yukon, organised into clans and moieties, with territories along the coast and islands. Raven is central to Tlingit storytelling, and clan ownership shapes who may tell what.

A trickster and culture hero in many North American nations, each with distinct stories. Among the Karuk he steals fire; elsewhere he is a fool, a transformer or a teacher. He is not one shared figure.

A trickster and transformer in Tlingit and other Pacific Northwest traditions, credited with bringing light and with teaching people crafts. Raven is cunning, greedy and generous by turns, and is not a model of good behaviour.
A sacred figure in Lakota tradition who brings the pipe and the seven ceremonies and promises to return. She is honoured in living practice, and her story is neither a curiosity nor an entertainment.
In Wabanaki tradition, the woman whose body becomes the first corn, beans and squash. The story is told as a gift and a grief, and it ties food to work, memory and reciprocity.

The inherent right of a nation to govern itself. For Native nations it is a legal and political reality upheld in treaties and court decisions, though it has been repeatedly violated, and it shapes how their stories and lands should be treated.
